headline: Price says he asked the referee for his checkout after Clayton's counting jibe
standfirst: After beating Ryan Searle 10-7, Gerwyn Price said he was not at his best in Wolverhampton and explained a 145 checkout mix-up that drew a joke from Jonny Clayton.
body: Gerwyn Price reached the Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals for the sixth time on Wednesday, but he left Wolverhampton talking about his counting rather than his 103 average. Speaking to the media, including Dartsnews, after the 10-7 win over Ryan Searle, the Welshman said he still had more to give.

Price said he had played well early on and felt "really switched on", before slipping a little after the first break. He said he let Searle off in two legs, a 76 and a 68, but felt he took two of his own in return, so the result was fair.

He also admitted to some nerves at 4-1 up. Searle, he said, usually plays well against him, and he thought so himself as the players left the stage for the first break. "I always play well against him as well," Price added.

The talking point was a 145 checkout that was taken out after a miscount. Price said he did not count it himself: he asked the referee what he had left, and was glad the answer was 88. Clayton then texted him, joking about who was the worst counter in Wales, according to Dartsnews.

Price was frank about his form at the tournament. He described his second group game as "absolutely rubbish" and said he had not brought his very best against Searle, but he promised to find another gear. He also said longer formats suit him, and that the early first-to-five games can feel like tossing a coin.
His quarter-final opponent is Niko Springer, who beat Rob Cross 10-8 earlier in the evening.
